cues.text: Customers ask: can you fix this? Here is how to know if it is easy, if the tailor must decide, or if it usually cannot be done.
Green means easy. Hemming pants, skirts, and jeans.
Taking in a waist, and shortening sleeves that do not have working buttons.
Sewing on buttons, fixing a seam, and replacing a zipper. You can take all of these.
Yellow means the tailor decides. Making something longer or bigger depends on hidden fabric.
Jacket sleeves with real buttonholes are hard to shorten. Shoulders, linings, and gowns are tailor jobs.
Leather, beads, sequins, and holes in the middle of the fabric also need the tailor to look first.
Red means usually no. Making something two or more sizes bigger.
Making it longer when there is no extra fabric, an invisible fix on thin fabric, or big changes to shoulders.
Not sure? Take a photo, write the question on the ticket, and say: our tailor will check and call you.
